```{=html}
<div>
<span style="font-family: Georgia, Times New Roman, serif;">Hi everyone!</span></div>
<div>
<br /></div>
<div>
<span style="font-family: Georgia, Times New Roman, serif;">An important part of being a researcher is conveying what you learn to others. &nbsp;The way mathematicians convey their results to colleagues is to write articles, which nowadays are posted on the <a href="http://arxiv.org/list/math/recent" target="_blank">arXiv</a>&nbsp;and submitted for publication in journals. &nbsp;In a journal, an article is ideally peer-reviewed to check for correctness and then published once any issues are corrected. &nbsp;</span></div>
<div>
<span style="font-family: Georgia, Times New Roman, serif;"><br /></span></div>
<div>
<span style="font-family: Georgia, Times New Roman, serif;">This system works well for mathematicians to convey topics to other mathematicians who have a similar background of knowledge as themselves. &nbsp;However, the size of the audience for these specialized journal articles is limited. &nbsp;For example, if I try to talk to other research mathematicians <i>in my own department</i>&nbsp;about our recent results, this is a non-trivial undertaking. &nbsp;</span></div>
<div>
<span style="font-family: Georgia, Times New Roman, serif;"><br /></span></div>
<div>
<span style="font-family: Georgia, Times New Roman, serif;">I think that it is our duty as mathematicians to share our understanding with as wide an audience as possible, and I think that creating and maintaining a blog is one good way to try to explain my research to a wider audience. &nbsp;I have been hoping to do this for a while and I figured that I would start with my most recent joint work on <a href="http://arxiv.org/abs/1308.0572" target="_blank">simultaneous core partitions</a>&nbsp;</span><span style="font-family: Georgia, 'Times New Roman', serif;">with Brant Jones and </span><a class="g-profile" href="http://plus.google.com/103061162497127117651" style="font-family: Georgia, 'Times New Roman', serif;" target="_blank">+Drew Armstrong</a><span style="font-family: Georgia, 'Times New Roman', serif;">. &nbsp;I may just have gotten <a href="https://www.google.com/search?q=a+round+tuit&amp;tbm=isch" target="_blank">a round tuit</a>.</span></div>
<div>
<span style="font-family: Georgia, Times New Roman, serif;"><br /></span></div>
<div>
<span style="font-family: Georgia, Times New Roman, serif;">I realize that even when I try to convey these ideas, it will not make sense to everyone. &nbsp;But I expect this to be a learning experience for me as well as for you. &nbsp;If you have any questions about the topics involved, leave a comment and I will try to answer your questions by providing external links or writing additional blog posts.</span></div>
<div>
<span style="font-family: Georgia, Times New Roman, serif;"><br /></span></div>
<div>
<span style="font-family: Georgia, Times New Roman, serif;">I would encourage other researchers to broaden their audiences as well, be it in research mathematics, mathematics education, or any other field. &nbsp;I think it is good for the researcher to try to convey their ideas to a wider field, and good for the public to see what it is that we do. &nbsp;I see this as part of a larger project, similar to&nbsp;<a class="g-profile" href="http://plus.google.com/107135522210834007871" target="_blank">+Dana Ernst</a>'s <a href="https://plus.google.com/u/0/107135522210834007871/posts/dhaPmhY8F8J" target="_blank">recent post</a>&nbsp;about making a "Science Gist" for mathematics. &nbsp;</span></div>
<div>
<span style="font-family: Georgia, Times New Roman, serif;"><br /></span></div>
<div>
<span style="font-family: Georgia, Times New Roman, serif;">Onward and upward!</span></div>

```
